A) Introduction: John Shirley, on behalf of the property owner, is requesting rezoning of property
located at 901- 903 West Lamar Alexander Parkway, Parcel ID # 057F A 009.00, from Business
and Transportation to High Intensity Retail. Parcel is 0.45 acres in size.
The applicant is requesting to rezone the subject property from Business and Transportation to
High Intensity Retail in order to combine it with the adjacent parcel to the northwest (Parcel ID
057F A 003.00) for the expansion of the existing Aubrey's restaurant. The property is designated
Commercial on the Future Land Use Map; therefore, no Future Land Use Map amendment is
required. The proposed High Intensity Retail zoning is consistent with the adjacent properties to
the north and west, which are already zoned High Intensity Retail, and will create a more cohesive
zoning pattern for the combined property.
The Maryville Municipal Planning Commission recommended approval of the rezoning at their
meeting on August 17, 2026.

A) Introduction: The City of Maryville is requesting a change to the Future Land Use Map for
properties located on the west side of Robert C. Jackson Drive and the south side of Big Springs
Road, Parcels ID# 056 – 071.11 and 056-071.20, from Industrial to Commercial. Parcel 071.11 is
7.48 acres in size, and Parcel 071.20 is 2.78 acres in size. These parcels were previously one parcel
and were recently divided for City infrastructure on the smaller lot and commercial development
on the larger, corner lot.
The subject properties are currently vacant. The proposed rezoning from Industrial to Business and
Transportation will create a more consistent zoning pattern with the adjacent property to the south
and the properties located across Big Springs Road to the north, which are already zoned Business
and Transportation, the City's standard commercial zoning district that permits most commercial
uses by right. Extending the Business and Transportation district to the subject properties
represents a continuation of the existing commercial zoning pattern, rather than creating an isolated
zoning district, and will facilitate the property's future commercial development.
The Future Land Use Map designates the property as Industrial and the adjacent properties to the
south and north as Commercial.
The Maryville Municipal Planning Commission recommended approval of the requested change
to the Future Land Use Map at their meeting on August 17, 2026.

A) Introduction: Sterling Engineering, on behalf of the property owner, is requesting a change to the
Future Land Use Map for property located on the west side of Sherwood Drive, approximately 280
feet of West Lamar Alexander Parkway (Parcel ID 057K A 002.01) from Residential to Mixed
Use to allow for the commercial development of a hotel.
The parcel proposed for rezoning was subdivided from the Maryville Church of Christ property.
This area is currently vacant and is intended to be combined and replatted with the adjacent
properties to the north along West Lamar Alexander Parkway. The adjacent properties are
currently zoned Business and Transportation, a commercial zoning district that permits most
commercial uses by right. The proposed rezoning will create a consistent zoning pattern for the
combined property and facilitate its future development.
The Future Land Use Map designates the property and the surrounding area to the south as
Residential and the adjacent properties to the north as Mixed Use.
The Maryville Municipal Planning Commission recommended approval of the requested change to
the Future Land Use Map at their meeting on July 20, 2026.

A) Background
Purchasing Regulations are dictated by Maryville City Code, Section 5, Chapter 2 and the City of
Maryville Charter. To further set purchasing processes, the Purchasing Policy’s primary function is to
describe the roles and responsibilities required for the most efficient management of the purchasing
process. It is necessary to update policies as requirements & procedures change. This UPDATE
includes such things as:
• Updating purchasing thresholds by increasing minimum requirements for requisitions to
$3,000.
• Updating and more clearly defining the Purchasing Cycle, the Bid Process, & credit card
purchases.
• Updating sealed bid requirements to correspond with recent Maryville Municipal Code update
• (increasing minimum from $25,000 to $50,000).
• Updating the credit card purchase limits to $3,000.

A) Introduction: With the passage of the Transportation Modernization Act in 2003, TDOT has been
delivering transportation projects based on a fiscally constrained 10-year plan. As part of the annual
planning process for the 10-year plan, the Statewide Partnership Program (SPP) is a critical avenue
for local agencies like the City of Maryville to provide input on their priorities. Transportation
projects on state or federal routes that are being developed by local agencies are eligible for state
funding through the SSP.
SR-33 W. Broadway Avenue widening (from S. Cedar Street to Montvale Road) has been locally
managed and federally funded using an 80% federal / 20% local up through the PE-NEPA and PE-
DESIGN phase of development. Each year from 2023 to 2026, this project has been submitted for
inclusion in the SSP but has not been selected in previous years. The City continues to apply for
this additional funding.
